providers.title: Torsion gives zero divisors
providers.scope: An element of finite order m > 1 gives (1 - g)(1 + g + ... + g^(m-1)) = 0 with both factors nonzero. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Unique products exclude zero divisors
providers.scope: If G has the unique-product property, K[G] has no zero divisors for every field K. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Zero divisors from two labelled graphs
providers.scope: Two connected immersed labelled graphs with odd intersections of outgoing letter sets, in a group where closed paths have label 1, give alpha beta = 0 in F_2[G], with alpha, beta nonzero when the roots are separated. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A torsion-free group algebra with zero divisors (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There are a finitely presented torsion-free group G with a finite two-dimensional classifying space and nonzero alpha, beta in F_2[G] with alpha beta = 0; proved in the last lesson from the named statements (SURF), (SEP), (CELL 2) and (PL 3); the inputs (PI1), (COV), (CELL 1), (PL 1) and (PL 2) are proved in the course on cell complexes, fundamental groups and covering spaces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite projective planes
providers.scope: Counts of points and lines and their incidences in the projective plane over a finite field. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Prescribed types
providers.scope: Every letter lies in the types of np vertices on each side, and the types of a vertex of A and one of B share an odd number of letters. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Turn weights
providers.scope: The turn weights are 1/(q+1), p or 1, the proportions on A are at most the weights, and w(t,u) = w(ubar,tbar). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The squared-word estimate
providers.scope: The squared word weights of length h >= 3002 add up to at most e^(-h/300). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Girth conditioning by switchings
providers.scope: For large n some tuple of matchings has girth at least L = floor(c log n). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Prescribed edges
providers.scope: Conditioned on girth at least L, a further prescription holds with probability at most 1/(np - s - r_n). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Small diameter
providers.scope: With high probability every component has diameter at most D_0 L. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The bounded-pattern estimate
providers.scope: With high probability there is no system of at most K paths, total length between L and CL, with a pairing satisfying the reduction condition by at most I interval pairs and at most eps H unpaired occurrences; eps is chosen before K, C, I. Proved in the sixth lesson. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bounded cycle rank
providers.scope: The image graph of such a system has bounded cycle rank, at most two vertices of degree one, and boundedly many branch vertices. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Chains and multiplicities
providers.scope: Paths traverse whole chains, and every edge is traversed at most 2(C + K) times. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Stage counts
providers.scope: The edge and vertex counts of the multiplicity stages satisfy sum E_j = H and sum V_j <= H + iota. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A common grid
providers.scope: Simultaneous approximation of all comparison shifts by multiples of one block length s. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Joins
providers.scope: Every block occurrence takes part in at most one join, and s times the number of unjoined occurrences is at most b + o(L). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Link balance
providers.scope: A link component without self-links satisfies 2z <= S + b. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bins
providers.scope: Block words have bins between delta s/2 and a_0 s, and each bin d contains at most e^(2d - delta s) words. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fixed letters
providers.scope: The expected number of realizations of a stage with fixed letters is at most n^(V_j - E_j - k_j) e^(-sum d_i + o(L)). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Permitted letters
providers.scope: Count of the letter assignments of a stage through link components and bins. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The product over the stages
providers.scope: The product of the stage bounds is at most exp(-(delta/2) H + a_0 b + o(L)). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduced spherical arrangements
providers.scope: Disjoint disks on a sphere whose boundaries carry paths in the graph, with all occurrences paired by disjoint arcs into partners with inverse letters on distinct edges. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short closures
providers.scope: Every path without backtracking closes up to a cyclically immersed path by a path of length at most DL, when the diameters are at most D_0 L. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Planar intervals
providers.scope: The pairing of an arrangement cut into N' pieces consists of at most 6N' order-reversing interval pairs inside pieces. Uses (SURF).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Recursive planar separation
providers.scope: A planar multigraph with m vertices has at most C_sep m / sqrt K vertices whose deletion leaves components of at most K vertices. Uses (SEP).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Absence of arrangements
providers.scope: With high probability the random graph admits no reduced spherical arrangement. Uses (SURF), (SEP).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Closed paths have trivial labels
providers.scope: Every closed path in the graph has label 1 in the fundamental group of the cone complex. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cone pictures
providers.scope: Essential spheres and null-homotopies of path labels are represented by cone pictures. Uses (PI1), (COV), (CELL), (PL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Band surgery
providers.scope: In a cone picture of least length, partners traverse distinct edges. Uses (SURF), (COV), (CELL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Asphericity and root separation
providers.scope: Without reduced spherical arrangements, pi_2 of the cone complex vanishes and paths from the roots to other vertices have nontrivial labels. Uses (SURF), (PI1), (COV), (CELL), (PL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Asphericity
providers.scope: All higher homotopy groups vanish and the universal cover is contractible: a finite two-dimensional classifying space. Uses (COV), (CELL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The comparison theorem
providers.scope: Chain maps from a free augmented complex to an exact one exist over the identity and are unique up to chain homotopy. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The periodic resolution
providers.scope: The periodic resolution of a cyclic group of prime order is exact, and its cohomology with coefficients F_l is F_l in every degree. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Torsion-freeness
providers.scope: The group of the construction is torsion-free. Uses (COV), (CELL).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite presentation
providers.scope: The group is generated by the letters with the labels of finitely many closed paths as defining relators. Uses (PI1).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
